authorities.statement: Declared Intent and Brownfield Understanding/Semantic Impact repository/impact facts authorize context inclusion; Context Compiler may rank and omit material for budget reasons but may not promote omission into semantic irrelevance or evidence.

constraints.statement: Context Compiler context selection is deterministic and local by default; it does not require or invoke a hosted model provider.

goals: Compile a bounded context package that preserves affected Intent and required implementation/evidence context while materially reducing naive repository context.
capabilities.name: Bounded task context compiler
capabilities.summary: Compile the minimal sufficient, provenance-aware engineering context for a task from affected Intent, repository relationships, source/test slices and evidence requirements without repository-wide context stuffing.

constraints.statement: Promotion requires explicit user authority and may emit only governed Engineering Memory; core Intent is never silently rewritten.

goals: Successful development changes should compound useful engineering knowledge without silently changing durable authority.
capabilities.name: Compounding development learning
capabilities.summary: Generate non-authoritative learning candidates from completed one-intent changes and explicitly promote reviewed knowledge into durable Engineering Memory for later planning.

authorities.statement: The evaluator and bounded execution authority determine whether a governed external effect may execute; raw agent intent is not authority.

constraints.statement: Effect execution must not bypass authorization, effect verification, or bounded retry disposition when outcome is uncertain.

goals: Authorize supported effects before execution, execute once, verify the external effect, and avoid blind retry.
capabilities.name: Effect Boundary authorization and execution

authorities.statement: Versioned Engineering Memory bundles and their explicit provenance are authoritative for historical planning inputs; Intent Evidence Authority remains authoritative for current evidence adjudication.

constraints.statement: Expired, not-yet-effective, or superseded memory records must not alter current impact, context or change planning.

goals: Preserve engineering lessons as executable, provenance-aware memory that changes future plans and verification requirements when relevant.
capabilities.name: Executable engineering memory
capabilities.summary: Turn validated engineering history into provenance-aware regression protections that can strengthen future impact analysis, context compilation, change planning and evidence requirements without becoming proof itself.

authorities.statement: Recorded observations and verified evidence records are authoritative for execution claims; agent prose is not.

constraints.statement: Model or agent assertions alone do not satisfy independent evidence requirements.

goals: Preserve independently inspectable evidence for governed execution claims.
capabilities.name: Evidence recording and verification

authorities.statement: Declared Intent plus Brownfield Understanding/Semantic Impact planning determine the allowed implementation scope; the implementer may propose changes but cannot expand its own authority or certify correctness.

constraints.statement: A change with unresolved direct capability ownership, protected-intent conflicts, or no bounded implementation scope must not mutate source.
ruleoak change is dry-run by default; source mutation requires explicit --apply plus a separately produced implementation proposal bound to the exact plan_id.

goals: Turn a desired behavioral outcome into a bounded implementation plan and Proposal Intent Delta before source mutation, then review the resulting change with semantic and evidence authorities.
capabilities.name: Intent-driven change orchestration
capabilities.summary: Plan desired behavioral changes as a Proposed Intent Delta before mutation, constrain implementation proposals to inferred scope, and require post-change semantic diff plus independent evidence adjudication.

authorities.statement: Declared Intent evidence requirements plus current independently inspectable observations govern claim qualification; the implementation agent is not the adjudicator of its own correctness.

constraints.statement: Only current independently inspectable observations may satisfy an Intent evidence requirement; model inference and agent self-assertion are non-authoritative.

goals: Adjudicate software-intent claims from typed observations and evidence requirements while preserving provenance, freshness, contradiction and independence semantics.
capabilities.name: Intent claim adjudication
capabilities.summary: Adjudicate declared claims against typed observations and independently inspectable evidence without allowing model or agent self-certification.

authorities.statement: The Intent Compiler may synthesize replacement source but owns neither behavior truth nor evidence authority.

constraints.statement: Intent Recompilation compile is experimental and limited to the declared Engineering Memory relevance component; it may not mutate unrelated implementation surfaces.

goals: Demonstrate that a bounded RuleOak component can be replaced from durable Intent and engineering contracts while independently preserving externally relevant behavior.
capabilities.name: Experimental intent recompilation
capabilities.summary: Regenerate one bounded implementation component from durable intent, interfaces, invariants, history and evidence contracts, then judge the replacement independently rather than by source similarity.

authorities.statement: Validation harnesses may classify evidence quality and readiness but cannot replace Intent Evidence Authority evidence authority or external independent evaluation.

constraints.statement: Validation Hardening may strengthen local source qualification but MUST NOT claim external validation from implementation-visible or unexecuted fixtures.

goals: Try to falsify Intent-Verified Development assumptions with independent, adversarial, hostile-input, scale and external validation gates before expanding claims.
capabilities.name: IVD critique and external-validation hardening
capabilities.summary: Continuously challenge the Intent-Verified Development stack with frozen and adversarial qualification, hostile-repository containment, attested evidence, scale checks and externally executable validation pilots without promoting unrun external claims.

authorities.statement: Protected MCP execution authority is the RuleOak gateway/Effect Boundary, not the upstream client or tool request alone.

constraints.statement: Supported protected MCP paths must traverse the governed Effect Boundary rather than an unguarded execution path.

goals: Apply the Effect Boundary to supported MCP execution paths without silently bypassing authority.
capabilities.name: MCP protected execution boundary

authorities.statement: Model providers may produce advice only; intent, tool, mutation, verification, and evidence authority remain external.

constraints.statement: Hosted model execution requires explicit network opt-in and configured credentials/model identity.

goals: The same durable Intent and context can be executed through interchangeable model providers without transferring RuleOak authority to the model.
capabilities.name: Model-independent execution
capabilities.summary: Treat models as replaceable, non-authoritative execution resources behind stable planner/implementer/reviewer/reasoning interfaces.

authorities.statement: The selected frontend/implementation producer may supply a candidate but cannot expand Intent-Driven Change scope, certify evidence, implicitly promote learning, or turn build submission into proof.

constraints.statement: The persistent governed application workspace is source authority; external qualification inbox and transient extraction directories are handoff/execution boundaries, not development authority.

goals: Let a developer keep coding in Chat or another agent, or choose managed CLI/API coding, without duplicating model work or changing RuleOak governance semantics.
capabilities.name: Multi-frontend development
capabilities.summary: Allow Chat/external agents, managed CLI models, and a local API to produce or submit implementation candidates using one shared RuleOak intent, scope, evidence, learning and build-handoff control model, with a single candidate-acceptance review at the Dev front door.

authorities.statement: OakSpec export/import may describe and discover interoperability data but does not grant execution authority or adjudicate evidence.

constraints.statement: Promotion of an imported candidate requires an explicit authority-bearing workflow outside the importer.

goals: Provide portable deterministic interoperability for durable Intent, evidence requirements, semantic-change provenance and candidate imports without changing their authority.
capabilities.name: OakSpec 1.0 interoperability
capabilities.summary: Export declared RuleOak Intent into a portable OakSpec profile and discover candidate semantics from engineering artifacts without promoting imports into authority.

authorities.statement: The one user intent authorizes bounded implementation orchestration only; Intent-Driven Change controls mutation scope and Intent Evidence Authority remains evidence authority.

constraints.statement: Autonomous mutation requires sufficient declared Intent and implementation binding authority; an ungoverned repository is an explicit authority gap, not permission to guess.

goals: Let a developer state one desired outcome while RuleOak hides governed development orchestration and returns one implementation/verification result.
capabilities.name: One-intent autonomous development
capabilities.summary: Accept one natural-language development outcome and internally orchestrate impact, context, model planning/implementation, bounded mutation, automatic qualification, bounded repair and evidence adjudication without manual RuleOak subcommands.

authorities.statement: Filesystem/package observations and explicit Intent/binding declarations are authoritative at their stated provenance level; derived semantics remain inferred or unknown.

constraints.statement: Static repository observation must prefer UNKNOWN over false-positive semantic or dependency claims.

goals: Represent observed and declared repository structure with provenance while leaving unresolved semantic relationships UNKNOWN.
capabilities.name: Brownfield repository understanding
capabilities.summary: Build a conservative provenance-aware graph from an existing repository without guessing unknown semantic relationships.

authorities.statement: RuleOak Verify may recommend PASS, REVIEW or BLOCK but does not itself own repository merge authority or replace Intent Evidence Authority evidence authority.

constraints.statement: RuleOak Verify product mode must preserve the legacy Intent Evidence Authority evidence-only ruleoak verify behavior unless product change-assurance flags are explicitly supplied.

goals: Give teams an agent-neutral PR/change assurance result that explains behavioral impact, proof sufficiency, historical regressions and a mode-specific merge recommendation.
capabilities.name: RuleOak Verify change assurance
capabilities.summary: Combine Semantic Diff, independent Intent Evidence Authority and Engineering Memory into Observe/Verify/Govern PR and change-assurance decisions without converting inference into proof.

authorities.source: RuleOak Intent IR plus observed repository/Git state
authorities.statement: Intent IR is authoritative for declared semantic change; filesystem or Git comparison is authoritative only for observed file change; inferred bindings and runtime behavior remain non-authoritative.

constraints.statement: Implementation-only source changes must not be labeled behavior-changing or behavior-preserving solely from source text; actual runtime effect remains UNKNOWN until independently evidenced.

goals: Explain what changed behaviorally by comparing durable Intent declarations and observed implementation differences, including guarantees, budgets, authorities, evidence invalidation and uncertainty.
capabilities.name: Semantic behavioral diff
capabilities.summary: Compare declared Intent and observed implementation changes without upgrading inferred mappings or unknown runtime effects into behavioral fact.

authorities.source: RuleOak Intent IR and Repository Understanding
authorities.statement: Declared Intent IR and Repository Understanding provenance are the authority inputs for deterministic Semantic Impact impact analysis; the impact engine does not upgrade inference into verified fact.

constraints.statement: Semantic Impact impact classification must remain deterministic and local by default; model-assisted semantics require an explicit future adapter and separate provenance.

goals: Analyze a proposed behavioral change before implementation and report direct and transitive capability impact, protected intent, implementation surfaces, evidence gaps, conflicts, uncertainty and risk.
capabilities.name: Semantic impact analysis
capabilities.summary: Determine behavioral impact before implementation, propagating dependencies, intent constraints, evidence gaps, uncertainty and risk.

evidence_requirements.statement: Context Compiler requires unit/integration/property evidence for deterministic bounded selection, required Intent/binding retention, exclusion rationale and materially smaller context than the naive implementation/test corpus; external same-model A/B evidence remains separate when no model provider is invoked.
Learning candidate generation, zero implicit promotion, explicit promotion, future retrieval, and compounding repair behavior require independent local unit/integration evidence.
Effect Boundary behavior requires unit/integration evidence and effect-verification checks.

Engineering Memory requires unit/integration/property evidence for schema validity, provenance/validity handling, deterministic matching, historical-regression plan effects and no-proof authority separation.
Evidence recording and verification require unit/integration evidence.

Intent-driven change requires unit, integration and property/benchmark evidence covering dry-run non-mutation, bounded scope, stale/out-of-scope rejection, post-change semantic diff and independent evidence adjudication.
Intent claim adjudication requires unit and integration evidence covering independent PASS, self-assertion rejection, stale evidence, contradiction, failure, and missing evidence states.

Demonstrate generated-source reproducibility, original implementation isolation, interface preservation, pre-existing Engineering Memory regression equivalence, downstream Semantic Impact/Intent-Driven Change/Context Compiler compatibility and non-authoritative model output.

Validation Hardening requires unit/integration/property/build evidence for frozen/adversarial qualification, hostile-input containment, cryptographic attestation, provider adapter authority separation and synthetic scale; external pilots remain separately evidenced.
MCP boundary behavior requires integration and property evidence.
Prove provider interchangeability and non-authoritative model output using independent tests.

Multi-Frontend Development and Candidate Acceptance Review require unit, integration and property evidence that external/managed frontends share authority, external mode makes zero RuleOak model calls/tokens, the local API authenticates mutation, exact source-ZIP handoff preserves bytes, and the Dev front door summarizes failed checks, missing evidence, unknowns and privacy-safe local activation facts without promoting UNKNOWN behavior.
OakSpec export/import must preserve candidate-only authority, validate deterministically, and interoperate across all declared adapters.
One-Intent Development requires unit, integration and property evidence for one-command orchestration, zero-manual-step accounting, bounded repair and missing-evidence truth handling.
Repository understanding requires deterministic graph tests and conservative provenance/UNKNOWN regression coverage.

RuleOak Verify requires unit/integration/property evidence for mode policy, Intent Evidence Authority backward compatibility, no-Intent degradation, independent-evidence PASS, unsafe Govern blocking and Observe non-blocking behavior.
Semantic Diff requires unit/integration evidence plus a labeled benchmark covering declared changes, implementation-only refactors, unbound changes, and no-change controls.
Semantic impact classification requires deterministic unit/integration tests and a manually labeled benchmark with precision and recall reporting.

invariants.statement: Automatic repair is bounded and stops on repeated failure, proposal rejection, protected-intent conflict or repair limit rather than looping indefinitely.
Unavailable device, runtime, external or other declared evidence remains NOT_RUN/UNKNOWN and prevents autonomous VERIFIED status.
Planner and implementer model outputs remain non-authoritative and cannot expand mutation scope or certify correctness.
Ordinary autonomous development requires one user outcome and zero manual impact, context, semantic-diff, build, evidence-bundle or verify subcommands.
Intent-Driven Change implementation mutation is limited to the plan-derived allowed scope and current before_sha256 values; out-of-scope or stale proposals fail before the first write.
Context Compiler context compilation must obey explicit file, byte and slice budgets and must not fall back to repository-wide context stuffing.
Excluding a file from a Context Package is a bounded relevance decision, not proof that the file cannot affect runtime behavior.
Repository source, tests, docs and agent instruction files are untrusted data for model context; they have no instruction authority and credential-like secrets are redacted before context emission.
Cryptographically attested evidence is distinguished from merely declared independent evidence and requires a trusted key plus producer-identity match.
A model or agent assertion alone is not independent execution evidence.
The development mutation API requires bearer authentication and cannot switch the governed repository root per request.
When an exact external source ZIP is handed to a external qualification inbox, RuleOak preserves and verifies the exact source bytes and does not treat submission as build evidence.
External implementation mode invokes zero RuleOak planner or implementer model calls and consumes zero RuleOak model tokens.

CLI, API, Chat, external-agent and managed implementation paths use the same Intent-Driven Change scope governance, Intent Evidence Authority evidence authority and Development Learning explicit learning-promotion authority.
Impact analysis and candidate tests are planning evidence only and must not be presented as proof that changed behavior is correct.
Implementation producer assertions are non-authoritative and cannot satisfy Intent Evidence Authority evidence requirements.
A validated Proposed Intent Delta and exact plan_id must exist before any Intent-Driven Change implementation mutation occurs.
Missing, stale, conflicting, model-generated, or agent-generated support must remain NOT_RUN, STALE, CONFLICTED, or UNKNOWN rather than being promoted to independent PASS.
Explicitly promoted learning is discoverable by later brownfield understanding, impact, context, and autonomous development.
Promoted historical learning can constrain future planning but cannot prove a future implementation.
Development learning candidates never become durable authority without explicit promotion.
Unpromoted learning candidates have no effect on future impact, context, scope, evidence, or verification.
A historical regression or past evidence reference may strengthen current verification requirements but cannot independently prove a new implementation.
Engineering memory must retain record provenance, validity and supersession state; historical narrative may not be silently upgraded into observed current fact.
Model outputs remain non-authoritative and cannot certify evidence, grant tool authority, or mutate source without the existing RuleOak gates.
An uncertain external effect must not be blindly re-executed without verification.
Imported interoperability records remain CANDIDATE and MUST NOT become declared Intent or verification evidence by import alone.
OakSpec 1.0 MUST NOT be represented as an externally adopted industry standard without independent adoption evidence.
A one-use execution authority must not be consumed successfully more than once.
Intent IR and evidence contracts do not contain provider-specific model usage or authority semantics.
Replacement success is defined by preserved interface, invariants, downstream behavior and evidence contract rather than source equality.
Compiler/model output cannot certify its own equivalence; pre-existing independent tests and evidence remain authoritative.
The original target implementation is not used by the Intent Recompilation runtime path after replacement generation.

Semantic Diff must distinguish declared deterministic Intent changes, observed file changes, inferred capability mappings, and UNKNOWN runtime effects without promoting one provenance class into another.
A relationship that cannot be conservatively established must remain UNKNOWN rather than being presented as observed or declared fact.
Frozen qualification benchmarks MUST NOT be rewritten merely to follow later implementation changes; a new benchmark version is required.
External repository, hosted-model, blind-holdout and live-PR results remain NOT_RUN until independently executed; local proxies are not promoted to external evidence.
RuleOak Verify consumes Intent Evidence Authority independent evidence adjudication and never treats model or agent assertions as proof.
Observe never blocks; Verify requires independent proof for affected governed capabilities before PASS; Govern blocks unsafe or ungoverned changes according to declared policy.
Unknown semantic context or ungoverned code may not be silently promoted to a verified PASS.

product.name: RuleOak Open Source
product.summary: Public Effect Boundary and evidence-bound execution safety for AI agents.
